original_value: Multiplex lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA) is largely used for point-of-care testing to detect different pathogens or biomarkers in a single device. The increasing demand for multitargeting diagnostics requires multi-informative single tests. In this study, we demonstrated three strategies to upgrade standard multiplex LFIA to multimodal capacity. As a proof-of-concept, we applied the strategies to the differential diagnosis of Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infection, a widespread pathogen, for which conventional multiplex LFIA testing is well-established. In the new two-parameter LFIA (x2LFIA), we exploited color encoding, in which the binding of multiple targets occurs in one reactive band and the color of the probe reveals which one is present in the sample. By combining the sequential alignment of several reactive zones along the membrane of the LFIA strip and gold nanoparticles and gold nanostars for the differential visualization, in this demonstration, the x2LFIA can furnish information on HIV serotype and stage of infection in a single device. Three immunosensors were designed. The use of bioreagents as the capturing ligand anchored onto the membrane or as the detection ligand labelled with gold nanomaterials affected the performance of the x2LFIA. Higher detectability was achieved by the format involving the HIV-specific antigens as capturing agent and labelled secondary bioligands (anti-human immunoglobulins M and protein G) as the probes.

result.paraphrase: Multiplex lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA) is widely used for point-of-care testing to identify multiple pathogens or biomarkers with a single device. The growing need for multitarget diagnostics calls for single tests that provide multiple kinds of information. In this study, we showed three approaches for upgrading standard multiplex LFIA to multimodal capability. As a proof of concept, we applied these approaches to the differential diagnosis of Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infection, a common pathogen for which conventional multiplex LFIA testing is already well established. In the new two-parameter LFIA (x2LFIA), we used color encoding so that multiple targets bind within one reactive band and the probe color indicates which target is present in the sample. By combining sequential alignment of several reactive zones along the LFIA strip membrane with gold nanoparticles and gold nanostars for differential visualization, the x2LFIA in this demonstration can provide information on HIV serotype and stage of infection in a single device. Three immunosensors were designed. The performance of the x2LFIA was influenced by whether the bioreagents were used as capturing ligands anchored to the membrane or as detection ligands labeled with gold nanomaterials. The highest detectability was obtained with the format using HIV-specific antigens as the capturing agent and labeled secondary bioligands (anti-human immunoglobulins M and protein G) as probes.
